case_name: Shankar Alias Kallu v State of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

28 February 1979
Cr.A. No. 182 of 1972.
The Judgment was delivered by: FAZAL ALI, J.
1.  In this appeal u/s. 2(a) of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970 the appellant has been convicted u/s. 302 IPC and has been sentenced to imprisonment for life and is directed against the judgment of the Madhya Pradesh High Court. We have perused the judgment of the High Court. So far as the prosecution case is concerned, we are satisfied that the case has been fully proved by the prosecution. The main witnesses relied upon are PW 2 and 4. We have perused the evidence of these witnesses and we do not find any reason to disbelieve their evidence.

facts: In this appeal u/s. 2(a) of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970 the appellant has been convicted u/s. 302 IPC and has been sentenced to imprisonment for life
The main witnesses relied upon are PW 2 and 4
The occurrence took place suddenly without any premeditation while the deceased along with the accused and others had just finished their meals
issues: What is that exact nature of the offence committed by the appellant
court_reasoning: On the prosecution case itself, the occurrence took place suddenly without any premeditation while the deceased along with the accused and others had just finished their meals
There can however be no doubt that he must be deemed to have the knowledge that death may be caused by his act
holding: The conviction of the appellant from one u/s. 302 to that of u/s. 304 (II) and reduce the sentence from life imprisonment to seven years R.I.
